findings.title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is null/empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar (handleNewBooking now sets `null` in that case). The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Any Google Meet booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar will throw. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and fell back to Cal Video. It should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references no longer persist credentialId
findings.body: The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video results kept their own credentialId. The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, which drops it for video results. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling a booking will no longer delete the Daily/Zoom/etc. meeting. Update and reschedule lookups that rely on the reference credential are affected too. The ternary should keep `result.credentialId` in the non-calendar branch.

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The following `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so collective hosts who do have calendars never get an event. This is exactly the scenario the PR is meant to fix. The array should be initialised to `[]` (not `null`) and the team destination calendars concatenated into it. The in-place `push` onto an array that is also exposed on `evt` is also fragile.

findings.title: Unrelated change inverts organization slug / requestedSlug logic
findings.body: The original code set `slug` only when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` and `requestedSlug` only when billing was enabled. The new code sets `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true, so with billing on the org gets its final slug immediately without payment/verification. With billing off, no slug is set at all. This flips the behaviour and has nothing to do with destination calendars. It looks like an accidental or merge-leftover change and should be reverted.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses undefined calendarId when no destination matches
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is now `undefined` when no destination calendar matches the credentialId. The insert falls back to `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. The patch then targets an undefined calendar and fails, or a required-parameter error is raised, so the description with the Meet link is never updated. Previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`. The same resolved id should be used for both calls.

findings.title: Destination calendars without credentialId no longer used when creating Google events
findings.body: The target calendar is now chosen only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. EventManager still handles destination calendars that have no credentialId by creating the event with each credential of the matching integration. For those legacy destinations nothing matches, so Google events are always created in `primary` instead of the configured `destination.externalId`. This is a regression for existing single-host users. The code should fall back to the main destination calendar's externalId when no credentialId match exists.

findings.title: Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent is dead logic
findings.body: The expression is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In the else branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the `find` compares against a falsy value and always returns `undefined`. The old fallback to the event's destination calendar externalId is gone. `updateEvent` now calls `events.update` with `calendarId: undefined` for references lacking externalCalendarId, which fails. `deleteEvent` (line 317) silently uses `primary`. The fallback should use the main destination calendar, e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

findings.title: CalDAV creates no event for second host's credential in collective events
findings.body: `createEvent` filters the account's calendars by the first (main host) destination calendar's externalId. EventManager now calls `createEvent` once per host credential, passing the whole destination list. For a second host's CalDAV credential, none of its calendars match the main host's externalId, so the filtered list is empty, `Promise.all([])` resolves, and `createEvent` returns success without creating anything. That host silently gets no calendar event. The method needs to use the destination calendar belonging to the credential being used (as Google does with `credentialId`).

findings.title: Office365/Lark use the first host's calendar id with every host's credential
findings.body: Both services take `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId` as the calendar id, regardless of which credential the call is made with. In a collective event with multiple hosts, EventManager invokes `createEvent` per host credential. Office365 then POSTs to `/me/calendars/<host A's calendar id>/events` using host B's token, which gets a 404/403 or lands in the wrong calendar. Lark's `createEvent` and `createAttendees` do the same with `calendarId`. The new `credentialId` argument (added to the interface) is ignored, so multi-host support only works for Google.

findings.title: Unrelated loadUsers rewrite changes behavior and drops the organization select
findings.body: The `loadUsers` refactor is unrelated to destination calendars and alters behavior. For dynamic groups it no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, so anything downstream reading `user.organization` for dynamic users loses data. It now throws for an empty `dynamicUserList` instead of returning an empty list. The catch block converts every non-Http/Prisma error into a generic 500 "Unable to load users", which hides the real cause. This should be split into its own PR or reverted.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation block now runs once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring-cancellation branch (deleting every `updatedBookings` calendar event across all of the organizer's calendar credentials) now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. With N calendar references (the multi-host case) it runs N times, issuing duplicate deletes that can fail on non-Google calendars. It also only iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and `updBooking.references.find(...)` (first calendar ref only), so other hosts' events for the remaining recurring instances are still not removed. The bulk deletion should be hoisted out of the loop and cover all references and credentials.

findings.title: destinationCalendar changes from object to array in webhook payloads and public types
findings.body: Webhook payloads spread the `CalendarEvent` (`...evt`), so the `destinationCalendar` field delivered to subscribers silently changes from an object/null to an array. Within the PR it is also inconsistent: the BOOKING_REJECTED e2e now expects `[]`, while BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED still expect `null`. This is a breaking change for webhook consumers and for any other code or templates reading `calEvent.destinationCalendar.<field>`. It should be called out or normalised, and docs updated.

findings.title: No tests for multi-destination calendar create/update/cancel flow
findings.body: The PR rewrites how calendar events are created, updated and deleted across EventManager, CalendarManager, handleNewBooking, handleCancelBooking and several CalendarServices. This includes new DB credential fallbacks and per-credential calendar selection. The author states no tests were added. The regressions above (null destination, video credentialId, legacy destinations without credentialId) would be caught by basic unit tests for `EventManager.create` and `updateAllCalendarEvents`.
